findings.title: Lithuanian account TOTP step text replaced with Italian
findings.body: The `totpStep1` value is replaced with an Italian sentence ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:"). Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the account TOTP setup page. The value should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:"). The same copy-paste error appears in the login messages_lt.properties file.

findings.title: Lithuanian login TOTP step text replaced with Italian
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` is changed to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". Lithuanian users get Italian text on the login TOTP setup screen, and the adjacent Lithuanian lines (loginTotpStep2/3) show the file is meant to be Lithuanian. This should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text in the Simplified Chinese bundle
findings.body: The new `totpStep1` value uses Traditional characters and a full-width colon ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). The other lines in this zh_CN file are Simplified (e.g. totpStep2 "打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码"), so this should be Simplified Chinese ("在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：").

findings.title: Placeholder syntax changed to Java MessageFormat in an i18next bundle
findings.body: The key is rewritten from `{{0}}`-style to `{0}` and gets an ICU `{2,choice,...}` plural segment. Every other interpolated error key in this account UI bundle uses i18next's double-brace syntax (e.g. line 140 `'{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.`), and the UI renders messages with i18next. Single-brace placeholders will not be substituted, and unless an ICU plugin is configured the choice segment is shown literally, e.g. 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|...}.' Keep the `{{n}}` syntax and use plain plural wording here.

findings.title: Admin UI message switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
findings.body: The admin console bundle is rendered by the i18next-based React UI, which uses double-brace placeholders. This change to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus an ICU `{2,choice,...}` segment will leave the placeholders unsubstituted and may show the choice syntax verbatim. The same key in the server-side admin theme (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/admin/messages/messages_en.properties) is a different bundle, and this JS-side bundle should not be changed to match it.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() wraps read failures in RuntimeException, and verify() only catches IOException and rethrows MojoExecutionException. Any locale file whose derived `_en` counterpart is missing (for example, `duplicate_keys.properties` maps to a nonexistent `duplicate_en.properties`, which is why the test fixture had to be renamed) escapes the Mojo as an unhandled runtime exception with a stack trace rather than a Maven plugin error. Report this through MojoExecutionException, or record it as a message.

findings.title: Diff-offset computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: start (common prefix) and end (common suffix) are each computed independently and capped only by the individual string lengths, so they can overlap. When the sanitized output is shorter than the input and the matching prefix and suffix together cover all of sanitized, `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` receives a reversed range and throws. Instead of reporting the illegal HTML, the verifier crashes. Clamp end so that start + end <= sanitized.length() (and the same for value).

findings.title: Anchor regex also matches unrelated tags such as <abbr> and <address>
findings.body: The pattern `</?a[^>]*>` has no word boundary after `a`, so it matches any tag starting with the letter a (<abbr>, <address>, <article>, etc.). Such tags are then handled by the anchor-matching logic and reported as "Didn't find anchor tag <abbr>..." rather than as illegal HTML, which gives a misleading message. Use `</?a(\\s[^>]*)?>` or equivalent.

findings.title: Duplicate-key assertion weakened from exact match to hasItem
findings.body: The original test asserted that the result contains exactly the duplicate-key message (Matchers.contains). It now uses hasItem, which still passes if extra messages appear. The rename to duplicateKeys_en.properties did not require this loosening, so the test loses its ability to catch new spurious messages for this fixture.

findings.title: No test that a valid translation produces no messages
findings.body:
All four tests only assert that a specific error message is present. Nothing checks the negative path: a correct translation (matching anchors, allowed tags, `
`, choice/templateHelp placeholders normalized) should produce an empty result. Without that, false positives in the verifier, like the ones the PR's bundle edits were made to work around, would go unnoticed.

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde ...`). The literal 'n' will be visible at the start of that paragraph in the rendered email. Since this line is already being changed, the typo should be fixed in the same edit.
